LESSON: KINGS DAVID AND SOLOMON

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: The Bible: Selected Teachings
Topic 2.3: Kings David and Solomon

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Kings David and Solomon. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: how King Solomon, 1. Why did King Solomon fail in his leadership?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain what Kings David and Solomon means in simple pupil language
2. give 3 correct examples of Kings David and Solomon from Kenya
3. practise Kings David and Solomon in clear steps
4. apply Kings David and Solomon in one real-life situation this week

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: KINGS DAVID AND SOLOMON
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Kings David and Solomon helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: KINGS DAVID AND SOLOMON
Study Kings David and Solomon like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Explain what Kings David and Solomon means in simple pupil language

What this means
In this part you learn to explain what Kings David and Solomon means in simple pupil language. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain what Kings David and Solomon means in simple pupil language.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Kings David and Solomon” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain what Kings David and Solomon means in simple pupil language. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Give 3 correct examples of Kings David and Solomon from Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to give 3 correct examples of Kings David and Solomon from Kenya. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: give 3 correct examples of Kings David and Solomon from Kenya.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Kings David and Solomon in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can give 3 correct examples of Kings David and Solomon from Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Practise Kings David and Solomon in clear steps

What this means
In this part you learn to practise Kings David and Solomon in clear steps. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practise Kings David and Solomon in clear steps.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practise Kings David and Solomon in clear steps. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Apply Kings David and Solomon in one real-life situation this week

What this means
In this part you learn to apply Kings David and Solomon in one real-life situation this week. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply Kings David and Solomon in one real-life situation this week.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Kings David and Solomon” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply Kings David and Solomon in one real-life situation this week. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Kings David and Solomon is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Kings David and Solomon” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: explain what Kings David and Solomon means in simple pupil language)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Kings David and Solomon in your own words. (skill: give 3 correct examples of Kings David and Solomon from Kenya)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: practise Kings David and Solomon in clear steps)

Example 4: Show how “Kings David and Solomon” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: apply Kings David and Solomon in one real-life situation this week)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Kings David and Solomon to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain what Kings David and Solomon means in simple pupil language.
3. Practise this skill: give 3 correct examples of Kings David and Solomon from Kenya.
4. Practise this skill: practise Kings David and Solomon in clear steps.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Kings David and Solomon from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Kings David and Solomon: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Kings David and Solomon?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. how King Solomon, 1. Why did King Solomon fail in his leadership?
2. Why was King David a man after God’s own heart?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Kings David and Solomon means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain what Kings David and Solomon means in simple pupil language.
5. Be able to: give 3 correct examples of Kings David and Solomon from Kenya.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
